Healing

Wounded? Choose Healing, then your hero.

Select a spell slot, then your hero or portrait. Select the same slot again to cancel.

Spells need stamina and time to cast. Your target must be in range; an interrupted cast may not heal.

Controls depend on your keyboard, gamepad and camera settings. The in-game guide shows your current bindings.

Classic edition reference

These original pages describe classic mouse and keyboard controls. Use the guidance above for current settings and gamepad controls.

Healing spell

You can wounds sustained in combat by casting a healing spell.

This is done by clicking on the spell's icon at the right screen edge (currently highlighted), and then clicking on the character.

See the next screen for more about using magic and casting spells.

Spells (part1)

There are many different spells available in this game. Because it takes energy to cast spells, it diminishes your character's "Stamina" (this is indicated by the blue bar under the character's picture). To replenish "Stamina" your character needs to rest, (standing still and not moving or fighting.)

To cast a spell on any character, click on the spell's icon on the right edge of the screen, and then click on the character, or the character's portrait, if the target is one of your characters.
To cast a spell on yourself simply double-click on the spell's icon.

Spells (part2)

You can also cast spells via the keyboard:

To cast spell 1: <1> key.
To cast spell 2: <2> key.
To cast spell 3: <3> key.
To cast spell 4: <4> key.
To cast spell 5: <5> key.
To cast spell 6: <6> key.
To cast spell 7: <7> key.
To cast spell 8: <8> key.

Note: If you hold down the <ALT> key while pressing the spell key, you will cast the spells on yourself or on your nearest enemy (for various damage-dealing spells).

Features

When casting spells, don't forget about some basic rules.

Each spell has a range. If a character receives a command to cast a spell on a target out of that range, he'll try to get closer first.
Don't expect spells to have an immediate effect. Each spell takes a certain time to affect the target. The time depends on the spell's complexity and the character's health (it is difficult to cast spell with crippled arm).
Some spells affect targets for longer periods of time. But the effects are not cumulative. Casting multiple spells of the same type at the same character will have no additional effect; the targeted character will only be effected by the strongest spell cast.
